findings.issue: Binary provenance is self-recorded, not checked against backend handoff manifest. Any existing historical or diagnostic executable can be supplied as current server and accepted as immutable current candidate.
findings.required_change: Require and freeze the approved backend artifact manifest; compare each of four current role hashes and relevant Go source hash before any test/build. Bind historical ST04 binary to its separate approved hash. Alternatively use an explicitly reviewed immutable expected-hash manifest, not hashes calculated only from CLI files.
findings.regression: Supply swapped old server/current server or changed harness with otherwise stable files; execution must refuse before starting tests. Correct handoff succeeds.

findings.issue: Failure evidence is not robust to exactly the drift it detects. Deleting/unreading a binary triggers verify failure, then finally sha(path) raises before save, leaving manifest running and losing failure/not-completed evidence. sources/inputs/dist collection can fail similarly. Popen is outside the per-process try, so launch failure lacks process evidence.
findings.required_change: Make final evidence collection best-effort per field, recording unknown/error without replacing original failure; always persist failed manifest and not-completed list. Include Popen launch failure in structured process record. Prefer atomic manifest replacement so interruption does not truncate last checkpoint.
findings.regression: Inject missing binary during a stage and final inventory failure; final manifest must remain valid JSON, failed, preserve original error/stage, and list unfinished suites. Inject launch failure and verify process record.

findings.issue: run_command catches BaseException after launch but only records and rethrows. wait_owned cleans the tree only for TimeoutExpired; KeyboardInterrupt or other wait error can leave owned build/preview/server descendants running. Even timeout tree-kill errors bypass guaranteed follow-up cleanup.
findings.required_change: In exception/finally, attempt bounded cleanup of the specific owned process tree when terminal state is not proven; retain original error and separately record cleanup outcome/remaining unknown. Do not operate on unrelated processes.
findings.regression: Inject KeyboardInterrupt/non-timeout wait error and tree-kill failure; assert owned cleanup attempted, original error preserved, bounded exit handling and explicit unresolved state.

test_strength: Current Python6/Node2 cover pure ID validation, dist checks, exact command replacement and ordinary timeout cleanup. They do not cover main orchestration provenance, finalization failures or interrupted-live-child cleanup. The timeout test asserting spawn count1 inside run_command does not prove main never starts preview after build failure; add a main-level mocked sequencing regression.
limits: No claim of actual145 discovery or passing E2E.
No product-code finding; changes requested concern acceptance runner integrity and resource/evidence handling.
No change to original SLO, fixture timing gates, COMMIT long-tail status or real voice/Pilot readiness.

dependency_integrity_check.details: inputs() includes package/lock and top-level config, but not web/node_modules contents. tool_versions records only Node/npm version strings and three package.json version values; it does not hash actual executable/dependency code. Editing node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js or a transitive module while preserving package versions/lock will not be detected by current verify(). Node executable content is also not frozen.
dependency_integrity_check.required_resolution: Before calling this full runtime-input immutability, explicitly freeze/verify the resolved runtime dependencies and executable identities, or obtain a documented narrower provenance contract and report this as an unverified boundary. Avoid silently claiming package-lock proves installed bytes. Coordinate a bounded implementation so repeated verification does not itself distort workload timings.
dependency_integrity_check.regression: Change an installed runner/build dependency without changing version/lock; chosen integrity check must reject, or the report must explicitly describe the unsupported guarantee.
